speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: asked	the Minister for Transport (a) whether there are any further plans or measures to reduce the frequency of accidents caused by PMDs or electric bikes colliding with pedestrians; (b) how does the Ministry ensure that PMD users will avoid using roads; and (c) whether new measures will be introduced to ensure that all electric PMDs in use or being brought into Singapore have appropriate speed limiters and that all PMD users adhere to the prescribed speeds.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: asked	the Minister for Transport how can the Ministry improve the safety of pedestrians given the recent spate of accidents involving e-scooters.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan
text: asked	the Minister for Transport whether there has been an increase in cycling or the use of PMDs on footpaths by persons doing so in groups of two or more and whether such usage by groups is supported by the current design of our footpaths.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan
text: asked	the Minister for Transport whether the tendency of certain cyclists and users of PMDs to switch between footpaths and roadways is a danger to other road users and whether the Ministry considers it necessary to address this issue as part of its deliberations on policy about allowing cyclists and PMD users on footpaths.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: asked	the Minister for Transport what additional measures can be taken to ensure safety for pedestrians and those who use the e-scooter, especially in areas of high pedestrian traffic and on public roads.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: asked	the Minister for Transport (a) whether the Ministry can provide an update on the plan to allow users of PMDs to share the pavement with pedestrians in the light of recent accidents involving e-scooters; (b) whether the Ministry is considering making it compulsory for users of e-scooters or equivalent to buy insurance plans that cover third party liability and accident damage; and (c) what are the recourses available to victims who are involved in accidents with users of PMDs.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There are altogether eight questions which reflect the valid concerns of the public, particularly in light of a recent accident that occurred in Pasir Ris.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Like Members, I was most upset and saddened by the accident, and I hope that the injured person, Mdm Ang, will make a full recovery soon.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In the meantime, Police investigations are ongoing and, when they are completed, we hope to have a better understanding of the accident.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For off-road cases, Police records currently do not distinguish between accidents caused by PMDs or bicycles and other offences causing hurt.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Going forward, LTA, which is now the lead agency for active mobility, will be tracking these.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As Members know, when used safely and responsibly, bicycles and PMDs offer great convenience and benefits.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They are environmentally friendly, promote a healthy lifestyle and are affordable.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In many cities around the world, there is growing interest to use bicycles and PMDs to Page: 45 get around.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: City planners and administrators also see benefits in promoting their use.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: However, the careless behaviour of a small minority of users has caused accidents and led some members of the public to oppose their proliferation.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It would be unfortunate if we allowed the careless behaviour of this small minority to prevent the larger majority of responsible and considerate cyclists and PMD users from enjoying the benefits of such travel modes.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The sensible approach is to adopt measures that will help prevent accidents.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Earlier this year, the Active Mobility Advisory Panel, which comprises representatives from a broad spectrum of society, issued a list of recommendations on how this can be achieved.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The recommendations were wholly accepted by the Government and will be tabled for debate in Parliament soon.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Power-assisted bicycles, even if they meet these criteria, will not be allowed on footpaths.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Second, we will regulate the behaviour of cyclists and PMD users on public paths.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: All must observe a speed limit of 15 km/h on footpaths and 25 km/h on cycling paths.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They must also abide by a code of conduct.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For example, cyclists and PMD users must always give way to pedestrians, and slow down and be prepared to dismount when approaching crowded areas, such as bus stops.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Third, we have already stepped up our enforcement efforts.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Land Transport Authority had set up a dedicated team of Active Mobility Enforcement Officers, and since May this year, the team has been patrolling hotspots where many cyclists and PMD users share paths with pedestrians.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: These enforcement officers have issued advisories to over 700 cyclists and PMD users for unsafe behaviours.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is about 5% of those that they engaged.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In other words, what that means is that the vast majority of cyclists and PMD users have been observed to be riding safely and responsibly.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In addition, LTA has conducted close to 20 joint operations with the Traffic Police to clamp down on reckless riding behaviour, and will continue with such enforcement operations.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Fourth, we have also stepped up education efforts.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: LTA launched the Safe Riders Campaign in April this year.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Safe Cycling Programme, which will start by February next year, will strengthen previous campaigns by also educating cyclists and PMD users about the new rules and code of conduct.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We are also partnering the community to roll out the Active Mobility Patrol scheme in more than 20 constituencies, where we will mobilise volunteers to join in the education outreach.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: LTA has also engaged retailers of PMDs to educate them about the new rules and, migh It add, the penalties.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is so that they are aware of the criteria for devices that can be used on public paths and the consequences of selling illegal devices.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Some Members have asked if we should register bicycles and PMDs and mandate third party insurance.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In the end, they assessed that registration and compulsory insurance would be too onerous and costly for the vast majority of cyclists and PMD users who behave responsibly and safely.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: However, power-assisted bicycles, which travel on roads and are typically prone to modification, should be registered.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Cities with a strong culture of active mobility, like Amsterdam and Copenhagen, likewise, do not mandate registration or insurance.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Like in those cities, pedestrians in Singapore who are injured in accidents can obtain compensation by initiating civil lawsuits or through private settlements.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If the offender is prosecuted and convicted in a criminal Court, the Court will consider Page: 46 if compensation to the victim should be paid.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The new rules and enforcement and education efforts will help to build a culture of responsible and safe sharing of space.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In many cases, safety is also about practising common sense, for example, by using paths in single file when the path is narrow, slowing down in crowded areas and not switching between footpaths and roads suddenly.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Many densely populated cities, like Tokyo and Amsterdam, have demonstrated that cyclists and pedestrians can co-exist harmoniously in the same space.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: [Pursuant to Standing Order No 22(3), provided that Members had not asked for questions standing in their names to be postponed to a later Sitting day or withdrawn, written answers to questions not reached by the end of Question Time are reproduced in the Appendix.] Page: 47
